scope: exact algebraic evanescent/pole sensitivity theorem for 4D numerator oracle plus D-dimensional loop measure

theorem.general: If N(delta)=sum_j N_j delta^j and M(delta)=sum_k A_k delta^k, then C_r=[delta^r](N M)=sum_j N_j A_{r-j}.

simple_pole.consequence: The leading simple-pole residue is protected against positive-delta numerator orders, but the finite remainder is not fixed by a 4D numerator oracle when A_-1 is nonzero.

double_pole.consequence: For double or higher poles, subleading pole coefficients as well as finite terms can be evanescent-sensitive.

theorem.no_pole: If the relevant discontinuity has no Laurent pole, the pole-times-evanescent mechanism does not obstruct its finite coefficient at that order; other matched-observable/scheme issues may remain.

parent_authority.paper: Giacchini, de Paula Netto, Shapiro, Phys. Rev. D 102, 106006 (2020), arXiv:2006.04217
parent_authority.authority_fact: The underlying calculation is formulated at arbitrary D and only later takes D->4 for the pole coefficient; intermediate coefficients contain explicit D dependence, including D-4 factors.
parent_authority.interpretation: A four-dimensional oracle cannot license N_{j>0}=0.

next_gate: Classify the corrected Iteration-296 bubble Laurent structure under this theorem; if its discontinuity is pole-free, the pole-times-evanescent obstruction does not apply to that finite cut at this order. Full same-parent finite effective-action authority still requires D-dimensional numerator continuation or explicit scheme conversion before promotion.
